metadata.title: Cutoff-relevant full-text evidence additions and corrections
metadata.missing_value_rule: Use 'not reported' when the full text does not state a value; do not infer it from examples or context.
metadata.evidence_basis: Methodological and evaluative claims were extracted from the complete supplied PDFs/text, not from abstracts. Bibliographic status was checked against the official arXiv API, Crossref, publisher DOI records, or ACL Anthology as applicable.
metadata.reviewer_separation_rule: Author-reported claims and limitations are stored separately from reviewer-identified validity concerns.
metadata.muse_handling: Muse was not duplicated here because research/master_evidence.json already contains matveyenko_2026_muse with DOI 10.18653/v1/2026.acl-industry.131.
important_corrections_to_master: The four arXiv-only records in this file were not verified as peer reviewed by the cutoff and must not be labeled peer reviewed.
None of the six systems is a multi-agent architecture; each is a single-model or multi-stage non-agent workflow, sometimes compared across multiple independently run models.

Agreement Is Not Quality reports 2,560 source messages, 2,494 messages after trigger-phrase removal for LLM coding, and 2,210 eligible messages in its main agreement table without reconciling the last reduction in the inspected full text.
Human-LLM Collaborative Inductive Coding reports mean pairwise human Jaccard 0.52 on 289 triple-coded messages; the remaining 2,271 validation messages were single-coded after calibration.

evidence_records.Full citation: Katz, Andrew; Coloyan Fleming, Gabriella; Main, Joyce B. 2026. Thematic analysis with open-source generative AI and machine learning: a new method for inductive qualitative codebook development. Humanities and Social Sciences Communications 13, 209. https://doi.org/10.1057/s41599-026-06508-5.
evidence_records.Title: Thematic analysis with open-source generative AI and machine learning: a new method for inductive qualitative codebook development
evidence_records.Authors: Andrew Katz; Gabriella Coloyan Fleming; Joyce B. Main
evidence_records.Venue: Humanities and Social Sciences Communications, volume 13, article 209
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: GATOS simulation-validation line; cites and contrasts earlier LLM-assisted thematic-analysis workflows but uses newly generated synthetic data.
evidence_records.Research objective: Test whether an open-weight, multi-stage NLP/LLM workflow can recover themes deliberately embedded in three synthetic social-science response datasets and thereby support inductive codebook development at scale.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: Selected steps of thematic analysis for inductive qualitative codebook development; the authors explicitly state that GATOS is not intended to replicate reflexive thematic analysis.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Research-question-conditioned atomic summary extraction, embedding and dimensionality reduction, clustering, nearest-code RAG, sequential code creation/no-creation decisions, code clustering, and LLM theme naming, followed by matching against planted themes/subthemes.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: inductive codebook generation evaluated against deductively known planted themes
evidence_records.Domain: synthetic teammate feedback, organizational ethical culture, and return-to-office attitudes
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: synthetic; authors state data will be made available in the corresponding author's GitHub repository
evidence_records.Number of documents: 854 teammate-feedback responses; 823 ethical-culture responses; 1,110 return-to-work responses; 2,787 total
evidence_records.Number of participants: not applicable; the study used simulated responses and no human participants
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: 2,787 synthetic responses; extracted summary-point counts were 4,563, 4,176, and 4,748, respectively
evidence_records.Document length: means/medians: teammate feedback 194/180 words; ethical culture 129/95 words; return-to-work 131/97 words
evidence_records.Model family: Mistral, Llama, and WizardLM open-weight families plus an unspecified text-embedding model
evidence_records.Exact model/version: GATOS: Mistral-small-22b-2409 (also rendered once as Mistral-22b-2409); simulation: Llama-3.1-70B, WizardLM2-8x22B, Mistral-Nemo-12B, and Llama-3.1-8B; embedding model not reported in the inspected main paper
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: Research-question-conditioned extraction; nearest-neighbor RAG over typically k=2-4 existing codes; prompts decide whether coverage is sufficient and create a code/definition only when needed; a final LLM consolidates codes into themes; full prompts are referenced in supplementary material; temperature 0 is reported in the discussion.
evidence_records.Fine-tuning or adaptation: no fine-tuning reported; retrieval augmentation, embeddings, dimensionality reduction, and clustering are used
evidence_records.Human role: Researchers specify the research question and simulation criteria, inspect synthetic outputs, and manually classify reference-to-output matches as good, partial, or none; the number and independence of match raters are not reported.
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: one synthetic open-ended response, decomposed into atomic summary points before clustering
evidence_records.Generated outputs: summary points, embeddings/clusters, an inductive codebook with definitions, and a hierarchical theme set
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: The workflow retains summary points through clustering and nearest-code retrieval, but the paper does not report an explicit final theme-to-source quotation graph or participant-level provenance output.
evidence_records.Baselines: Planted synthetic themes/subthemes serve as the reference; prior systems are compared conceptually, but no human analysis of the same natural corpus and no alternative computational baseline are evaluated.
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: temperature 0 is reported; stochastic reruns, random seeds, and sensitivity replications are not reported
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: best-match embedding cosine similarity, code/theme counts, summary-point counts, and code-creation trajectories; the primary match assessment is manual good/partial/no-match classification
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: Research-team members judge whether each planted subtheme has a good, partial, or no match among generated themes and inspect synthetic-data realism.
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: descriptive counts and distributions only; no uncertainty interval or inferential comparison is reported for thematic recovery
evidence_records.Principal results: GATOS produced 249 codes/89 themes, 246/75, and 314/110 across the three datasets. It recovered 54/60 planted teammate-feedback subthemes as good and 6 partial; 52/64 ethical-culture subthemes as good, 9 partial, and 3 none; and 60/63 return-to-work subthemes as good and 3 partial. Every planted top-level theme had at least one good generated match.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: No empirical runtime, hardware, energy, or monetary cost is reported; the authors describe the workflow as computationally intensive at larger scales.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: The paper states that ethics approval and informed consent were not obtained because no human participants or human data were used. It argues that local open-weight models can reduce third-party transmission and model-version risks.
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: Supplementary prompts are linked through the article; synthetic data are stated to be made available at https://github.com/andrewskatz, but the paper gives no study-specific repository path or immutable release; exact embedding/clustering specifications are incomplete in the inspected main text.
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: Synthetic data may lack human nuance and remain in-distribution for later models; near-redundant codes persist; abstraction level, scale, iterative refinement, full interviews, and robustness to model/embedding/clustering choices remain unresolved.
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Reviewer interpretation: using LLM-generated responses with planted LLM-generated themes can make recovery easier through shared distributional priors even though different generator/analyzer models were used. The single planted theme universe assumes one correct interpretation, does not test minority/negative-case retention, and lacks independent rater reliability. Cosine separation between manual match categories is corroborative rather than a validated thematic-quality metric.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Extends Katz and collaborators' earlier LLM-assisted codebook work into an open-weight RAG/clustering workflow and directly compares its phase mapping with Dai et al., Qiao et al., and collaborative systems.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: A strong baseline for testing generator-analyzer distributional confounding, participant/source-disjoint validation, minority-case preservation, and source-linked evaluation on natural data.

evidence_records.Full citation: Liu, Alex; Esbenshade, Lief; Xiao, Michael; Tian, Victor; Zhang, Zachary; He, Kevin; Sun, Min. 2026. Agreement Is Not Quality: Blind Expert Verification of Human and LLM Qualitative Coding When Human Consensus Is Not Ground Truth. arXiv:2607.28890v1. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28890v1.
evidence_records.Title: Agreement Is Not Quality: Blind Expert Verification of Human and LLM Qualitative Coding When Human Consensus Is Not Ground Truth
evidence_records.Authors: Alex Liu; Lief Esbenshade; Michael Xiao; Victor Tian; Zachary Zhang; Kevin He; Min Sun
evidence_records.Peer-reviewed status: not peer reviewed as verified by the cutoff; no archival venue was identified
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not available; the official arXiv API does not supply citation counts; checked 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: UW/Colleague K-12 educator-AI family; reuses the hierarchical codebook and independent 2,560-message validation corpus developed in the companion inductive-coding preprint
evidence_records.Research objective: Test whether agreement with trained humans is an adequate proxy for qualitative coding quality by comparing human and LLM code sets through source-blind, source-symmetric expert verification.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: Deductive multi-label qualitative coding evaluated without presuming human consensus is ground truth.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Three trained humans and five focal LLMs apply a fixed 72-item hierarchical codebook; agreement metrics are triangulated with 855 randomized, anonymized pairwise code-set judgments from one independent education expert and Bradley-Terry ranking.
evidence_records.Domain: K-12 educator use of a generative-AI platform
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: restricted platform data; no public data release located in the inspected full text
evidence_records.Number of documents: 2,560 educator-AI messages from 500 conversations; 2,494 after excluding 66 platform-trigger phrases for LLM coding; the main agreement table reports 2,210 eligible messages without explaining the additional reduction
evidence_records.Number of participants: number of distinct educator users not reported
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: 2,560 messages; average approximately 2 codes per message is stated in the codebook description
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: potentially sensitive professional education-platform logs; PII removed before analysis
evidence_records.Model family: Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, and OpenAI GPT families
evidence_records.Exact model/version: Claude Opus 4.8; Claude Haiku 4.5; Gemini 3.5 Flash; GPT-4o; GPT-5.5; the paper says full API strings/access dates are in Appendix C, but Appendix C was not present in the supplied full text
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: Identical chain-of-thought structured prompt for every model, complete human-authored 72-code definitions, instruction to identify all relevant codes, JSON output, temperature zero or provider-minimum reasoning, no session memory, and one message per call.
evidence_records.Single-agent or multi-agent: multiple independently evaluated single-call models; no agent workflow
evidence_records.Human role: Three education-domain coders calibrate, write the coding protocol/definitions, and code the corpus; one independent doctoral education researcher with K-12 teaching experience performs blind verification.
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: one educator message and its multi-label code set
evidence_records.Generated outputs: deductive code sets, confidence scores, agreement profiles, blind preferences, source rankings, and a code-level division-of-labor typology
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: The verifier is shown the source message and two anonymized code sets for that same message; the study does not propose a persistent quote-to-code provenance artifact beyond message-level comparison.
evidence_records.Baselines: Three trained human coders, human-human agreement, LLM-LLM agreement, and five focal LLMs are evaluated symmetrically; three additional models coded the corpus but were excluded from verification because of verifier capacity.
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: Four focal models were rerun once under identical conditions; intra-model exact match and kappa were reported; the fifth focal model was not rerun; random seeds are not reported.
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: message-level Jaccard, directional hit rates, exact match, human-human and LLM-LLM agreement, Cohen kappa for repeat stability, multi-model consensus, and confidence-agreement association
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: 855 randomized blind comparisons: 555 human-vs-LLM, 210 LLM-vs-LLM, 85 human-vs-human, and 5 rare-code supplement pairs; choices were Set 1, Set 2, both adequate, or neither adequate.
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: Three trained coders (doctoral education, master's education, and education-minor/industry research backgrounds) plus one independent doctoral education/K-12 expert verifier
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: Human-human mean pairwise Jaccard approximately 0.52 on 284 overlap messages; no inter-verifier reliability because there was one verifier. Four repeated models achieved exact-match stability 71.1%-99.2% and kappa 0.871-0.995.
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: Binomial preference tests with 95% confidence intervals and Cohen h; Bradley-Terry model with bootstrap confidence intervals; position-bias test; point-biserial correlation between confidence and agreement; per-code descriptive endorsement analyses.
evidence_records.Principal results: Mean human-LLM Jaccard was 0.30 versus human-human 0.52. Of 515 decisive human-vs-LLM comparisons, humans were preferred 51.5% and LLMs 48.5% (p=0.537; 95% CI 0.470-0.559). Claude Opus and Gemini Flash were numerically preferred over humans but not significantly; GPT-4o and Claude Haiku were significantly less preferred. The Bradley-Terry ranking interleaved human and LLM sources. The paper classifies 6 codes as automatable, 16 LLM-assisted, 12 LLM-preferred, and 15 human-required.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: Institutional IRB approval is reported with institution redacted; PII was removed; enterprise API contracts prohibited training on submitted data; each message was a separate call.
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: The full text points to appendices for prompts, configurations, codebook, and detailed tables, but those appendices and a data/code availability statement were not present in the supplied PDF; raw platform data are not public.
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: One codebook and dataset; a single verifier; time-specific model rankings; temperature-zero/no-memory setup only; verification limited to a selected five-model subset.
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Reviewer interpretation: the source-blind verifier is independent of original coding but is still one normative judge, so the study demonstrates that rankings can diverge rather than establishing which interpretation is generally valid. Code-level automation categories are data-, model-, prompt-, and verifier-specific. The unexplained 2,494-to-2,210 analysis reduction and the statement that all humans coded the full corpus versus the companion paper's single-coder allocation require reconciliation.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Direct companion to Human-LLM Collaborative Inductive Coding; uses its final 72-item codebook and the same 2,560-message human-validation sample, so it is not an independent dataset replication.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: The strongest recent precedent for evaluation without a single human gold standard; an ARR contribution should extend it with multiple independent experts/stakeholders, participant/source coverage, provenance, and cross-domain validation.

evidence_records.Full citation: Liu, Alex; Sun, Min; Esbenshade, Lief; Xiao, Michael; Tian, Victor; Zhang, Zachary; He, Kevin. 2026. Human-LLM Collaborative Inductive Coding for Conceptualizing K-12 Educator AI Use. arXiv:2607.28889v1. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28889v1.
evidence_records.Title: Human-LLM Collaborative Inductive Coding for Conceptualizing K-12 Educator AI Use
evidence_records.Authors: Alex Liu; Min Sun; Lief Esbenshade; Michael Xiao; Victor Tian; Zachary Zhang; Kevin He
evidence_records.Peer-reviewed status: not peer reviewed as verified by the cutoff; no archival venue was identified
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not available; the official arXiv API does not supply citation counts; checked 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: UW/Colleague K-12 educator-AI family; creates the codebook and validation sample later reused in Agreement Is Not Quality
evidence_records.Research objective: Document an auditable, phase-specific division of labor in which LLMs help scale open, axial, and selective coding while researchers retain conceptual authority and trained humans validate the resulting instrument on independent data.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: Open, axial, and selective coding adapted from grounded-theory traditions; the authors explicitly state that the goal is codebook/instrument construction, not theory generation.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Overlapping conversational trios are independently passed to Claude for open-schema extraction, large-scale candidate labeling, and closed-vocabulary application; two researchers inspect raw text/output, memo and merge; three trained human coders calibrate and apply the codebook to an independent message/conversation-disjoint sample.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: inductive development followed by deductive human validation
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: restricted; raw conversations cannot be shared under the privacy agreement; coding results are available on request
evidence_records.Number of documents: 256 trios in the open-coding pilot; 9,352 trios in axial coding; 11,539 trios in selective coding; independent validation sample of 2,560 messages from 500 conversations
evidence_records.Number of participants: number of unique users represented in the analyzed samples not reported; the platform had more than 15,000 active educator users
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: approximately 45,000 educator and AI messages overall; 21,147 overlapping trios across inductive phases plus 2,560 validation messages
evidence_records.Document length: some conversations exceeded 500 messages; validation conversations ranged to 68 messages; trio token/word lengths not reported
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: potentially sensitive professional logs; some educator prompts contained pasted student writing
evidence_records.Exact model/version: claude-3-sonnet-20240229 for open/axial work; claude-3-5-haiku-20241022 for selective coding
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: One API call per overlapping educator-prompt/AI-response/educator-follow-up trio; no session memory; strict JSON schemas; expanded open schema; closed vocabulary with an 'Other' option and rationale in selective coding; prompts/codebook archived.
evidence_records.Single-agent or multi-agent: multi-phase single-model workflow; no agent architecture
evidence_records.Human role: Two researchers review raw data and model outputs, memo, decide all category definitions/merges/pruning, and review all 'Other' responses; three education-domain coders calibrate and apply the final instrument, adding codes the LLM-assisted phases missed.
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: overlapping three-message conversation windows for LLM-assisted development; individual educator messages for human validation
evidence_records.Generated outputs: candidate analytic labels, structured annotations, a 67-item preliminary hierarchical codebook, and a human-validated 72-item codebook in 19 categories and six domains
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: Researchers read raw data alongside LLM outputs and record rationales through memoing; conversation IDs and metadata exist, but the paper does not report a released quote-to-code-to-theme provenance graph.
evidence_records.Baselines: Independent conversation/message-disjoint human application of the generated instrument; no fully human codebook-development baseline and no counterfactual no-LLM development arm.
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: each trio was processed independently; repeated stochastic runs, temperatures, seeds, and cross-model sensitivity tests are not reported
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: pairwise set Jaccard at item/category/domain granularity, code frequencies, and semantic distinctiveness/frequency used during pruning
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: Two researchers reviewed all 256 open-pilot outputs, a random 1,000 axial outputs, and all selective 'Other' responses. Three trained coders completed three calibration rounds and coded an independent 2,560-message sample.
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: Two codebook-development researchers; three validation coders with doctoral education, master's education, and education-minor/industry research backgrounds
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: Mean pairwise Jaccard 0.52 on 289 messages coded by all three, with reported range 0.46-0.55 across item/category/domain granularity; the remaining 2,271 messages were single-coded after calibration.
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: descriptive frequency distributions and pairwise set agreement; no confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, or independent codebook-quality judgment reported
evidence_records.Principal results: The LLM-assisted phases produced 67 items in 18 categories and six domains. Human calibration/application added culturally responsive teaching, foreign-language skill development, classroom management, class/school/community events, and school-district finance, yielding 72 items in 19 categories and six domains. The 2,560 validation messages received 5,237 code applications (mean 2.05 per message).
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: Institutional IRB approval is reported with institution redacted; platform terms allowed deidentified research use; PII was removed; enterprise APIs prohibited training on submitted data. The paper explicitly discusses pasted student-writing excerpts but treats them as part of educator messages under the IRB determination.
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: Full codebook, prompts, and replication scripts with synthetic templates: https://osf.io/ju59q/overview?view_only=96afb71945044b8794e113f9763cc74a; raw data restricted; coding results by request.
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: One platform; commercial model proposals are not strictly reproducible; human agreement can improve; observed requests do not establish classroom implementation.
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Reviewer interpretation: the process is strongly human-led, but LLM candidate labels can anchor the vocabulary without a fully human development comparator. Only a sample of axial outputs was reviewed; no reliability is reported for the two researchers' development-stage judgments. The model switch is argued away conceptually but not tested empirically. Minority/user-population coverage is not quantified even though five human-added codes reveal missed coverage.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Companion to Agreement Is Not Quality, which reuses the final codebook and the same 2,560-message validation corpus for model-versus-human evaluation.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Provides a realistic human-primary workflow and an empirical example of LLM-assisted phases missing emerging/minority contexts; an ARR study can prospectively measure participant-level coverage and anchoring against human-only development.

evidence_records.Full citation: Camporese, Maria; Massacci, Fabio; Gong, Yuanjun. 2026. LLMs for Qualitative Data Analysis Fail on Security-specific Comments in Human Experiments. In 34th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Program Comprehension (ICPC '26), 14 pages. https://doi.org/10.1145/3794763.3798172.
evidence_records.Title: LLMs for Qualitative Data Analysis Fail on Security-specific Comments in Human Experiments
evidence_records.Authors: Maria Camporese; Fabio Massacci; Yuanjun Gong
evidence_records.Venue: 34th IEEE/ACM International Conference on Program Comprehension (ICPC 2026)
evidence_records.Publication history notes: ICPC 2026, 2026-04-12 to 2026-04-13; arXiv v1 submitted 2026-04-12; within cutoff
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: Uses unpublished annotations supplied by the Papotti et al. security-experiment research line to reduce likely pretraining contamination.
evidence_records.Research objective: Determine whether four frontier/proprietary and open-weight LLMs can replace one human annotator for nine sparse, security-specific codes and whether progressively richer prompting improves replacement quality.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: Thematic analysis of free-text human-experiment justifications.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Fixed-code, binary deductive annotation of nine technical features/interpretations in short security comments; codebook emergence occurred in prior human work, while the present experiment evaluates automated code application.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: deductive in the evaluated LLM task
evidence_records.Domain: software security, vulnerability identification, and program comprehension
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: data and implementation released at https://zenodo.org/records/18742065
evidence_records.Number of documents: 263 free-text comments corresponding to vulnerability judgments on six code snippets; 13 codes were annotated and nine evaluated
evidence_records.Number of participants: number of Computer Science master's-student participants not reported
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: human-experiment and security-related comments; deidentification status not reported
evidence_records.Model family: OpenAI GPT, Anthropic Claude, DeepSeek, and Alibaba Qwen; GPT-4o used for prompt piloting
evidence_records.Exact model/version: GPT-5; Claude-4/Sonnet 4; DeepSeek-V3.2; Qwen3-Max; exact service snapshots/configuration dates not reported; GPT-4o interactive version used only to refine P3+
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: P1 task/context plus code names; P2 formal definitions and examples; P3 labels from other annotators; P3pilot asks for conflicting examples; P3+ adds human clarifications to contrastive cases. Models fill missing spreadsheet cells for the held-out annotator context.
evidence_records.Single-agent or multi-agent: multiple separately tested single-model annotation runs; no agent architecture
evidence_records.Human role: Four original annotators each coded one quarter and reviewed another annotator's portion; disagreements were discussed and reviewer-corrected labels were used as the comparison reference. Humans also supplied definitions, examples, and P3+ clarifications.
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: one participant comment with code-snippet/experiment spreadsheet context and one binary decision per code
evidence_records.Generated outputs: binary annotations for nine codes and spreadsheet-formatted results
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: Outputs are directly tied to source comment rows and code columns; no rationale/evidence-span requirement is reported for final annotations.
evidence_records.Baselines: The replaced human annotator and reviewer-corrected human labels; four LLMs; prompt-ablation sequence P1-P3+.
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: 4 LLMs x 4 prompt conditions x 4 replaced-annotator contexts = 64 annotation conditions; repeated stochastic trials and seeds not reported
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: precision, recall, accuracy, Cohen kappa/Heidke skill score as chance-corrected accuracy, per-code kappa, and token counts
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: Comparison against pre-existing four-human annotation/review workflow; qualitative failure-case inspection of a subset of model outputs
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: four human annotators plus reviewers; their names, qualifications, and security expertise are not reported in this paper
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: Human-reviewer agreement for the nine evaluated codes is approximately 0.93-0.98 in Table 4; final-prompt model kappa averages were 0.26 GPT-5, 0.30 Claude-4, 0.53 DeepSeek-V3.2, and 0.61 Qwen3-Max.
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: Wilcoxon paired tests for model and adjacent-prompt comparisons with Bonferroni threshold 0.017; descriptive per-code analyses
evidence_records.Principal results: Formal definitions improved pooled kappa from 0.37 (P1) to 0.42 (P2), while P3 fell to 0.35 and P3+ returned to 0.42. Improvements were not uniform across codes/models. Qwen3-Max performed best overall (kappa 0.61), but all systems showed severe code-specific failures; the paper concludes they should assist rather than replace security annotators.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: Token effort is plotted, but monetary cost, wall-clock time, and human prompt-development time are not quantified.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: The paper does not report ethics approval, consent, deidentification, participant privacy safeguards, or vendor data-retention terms for the underlying human-experiment comments.
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: Data and implementation: https://zenodo.org/records/18742065. Exact hosted model snapshots and repeated-run settings are not reported, and several candidate models were excluded because they could not reliably return the required tabular output.
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: One security experiment, nine codes, CS master's-student rather than professional-developer comments, model snapshot obsolescence, spreadsheet constraints/excluded models, and subjective prompt engineering.
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Reviewer interpretation: this is a well-motivated negative result for deductive annotation, not an evaluation of theme induction. Reviewer-corrected human labels remain a single reference and cannot establish interpretive validity. The unpublished-source strategy reduces but does not measure pretraining contamination. Manual public chat interfaces and absent stochastic repeats limit reproducibility, while ethics reporting is inadequate for human-experiment data.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: The annotations come from an unpublished experiment by the research group behind Papotti et al.; the present work deliberately avoids previously published annotations that models might have seen.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: Provides a hard-domain negative baseline and motivates evaluation of semantic shortcuts, domain specificity, contamination, and human-disagreement cases rather than relying on aggregate agreement.

evidence_records.Full citation: Liu, Yuhan; Zhou, Shuyao; Kaiser, Jakob; Colby, Ella; Okwara, Jennifer; Wang, Maggie; Rao, Varun Nagaraj; Monroy-Hernandez, Andres. 2026. How can LLMs Support Policy Researchers? Evaluating an LLM-Assisted Workflow for Large-Scale Unstructured Data. arXiv:2604.04479v2. https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.04479v2.
evidence_records.Title: How can LLMs Support Policy Researchers? Evaluating an LLM-Assisted Workflow for Large-Scale Unstructured Data
evidence_records.Authors: Yuhan Liu; Shuyao Zhou; Jakob Kaiser; Ella Colby; Jennifer Okwara; Maggie Wang; Varun Nagaraj Rao; Andres Monroy-Hernandez
evidence_records.Peer-reviewed status: not peer reviewed as verified by the cutoff; no archival venue was identified
evidence_records.Publication history notes: arXiv v1 submitted 2026-04-06; v2 posted 2026-04-07; v2 is the latest version as of cutoff
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not available; the official arXiv API does not supply citation counts; checked 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: QuaLLM lineage; adapts Rao et al.'s workflow for policy research and adds source selection, a practitioner interface/user study, chatbot-led interviews, and comparison with policy reports
evidence_records.Research objective: Evaluate whether a QuaLLM-derived workflow can provide policy researchers with fast, scalable, evidence-backed overviews from Reddit and chatbot-led interviews and how its themes compare with expert-authored policy reports.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: LLM-assisted thematic analysis as a complementary early-stage policy sensemaking method.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Hybrid template/content-analysis workflow: researchers define high-level categories, an LLM extracts quotes, generates bottom-up subthemes within categories, maps one code to each quote, counts quote prevalence, merges batched themes, and generates reports with selected evidence.
evidence_records.Domain: United States public opinion and policy research; climate change, social media/children, and economic impacts of AI
evidence_records.Dataset name: Study 1 Reddit interface data; Study 2 Academic Torrents Reddit corpus; Study 2 Prolific chatbot interviews; six authoritative policy reports
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: Reddit source archives are public; interview transcripts are not stated to be public; no project data/code release is reported
evidence_records.Number of documents: Study 2: 5,491,991 Reddit entries from 288 subreddits, yielding 122,191 relevant quotes; 1,058 completed interviews yielding 27,042 Q-A units and 16,029 retained human-message quotes; six reports
evidence_records.Number of participants: Study 1: 11 experienced policy researchers; Study 2: 1,058 completed U.S. adult interview participants, with 73 additional non-completers excluded; Reddit user count not reported
evidence_records.Approximate corpus size: Reddit: 5,491,991 entries and 122,191 retained quotes; interviews: mean 26.85 Q-A pairs and 1,493.03 words per conversation, with 16,029 retained quotes
evidence_records.Document length: Interview mean 1,493.03 words (SD 526.04); retained interview quote mean 22.1 words (SD 19.83); Reddit entry lengths not reported
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: Personal economic views and demographics in interviews; Reddit posts may contain identifiable or sensitive context
evidence_records.Exact model/version: Underlying analysis model reported only as GPT-4; subreddit relevance model gpt-4o-mini-2025-03-01; interview chatbot gpt-4o-2024-05-13
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: Structured multi-stage prompts for source relevance, nine high-level themes in Study 1, quote extraction, top subthemes, batch-of-500 theme generation/merge in Study 2, and one-code quote assignment. Relevance prompts were iteratively tuned against researcher labels until kappa 0.7; appendices reproduce prompts.
evidence_records.Fine-tuning or adaptation: no fine-tuning reported; QuaLLM is adapted through prompt and workflow changes
evidence_records.Single-agent or multi-agent: single-model multi-prompt workflow plus a separate interview chatbot; no multi-agent deliberation
evidence_records.Human role: Policy researchers define scope/select sources and evaluate the interface; one researcher calibrates source/quote relevance; two researchers review every report theme and three quotes per theme; two researchers and a public-polling expert synthesize Study 2 themes; a polling expert designs the interview protocol.
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: Linearized Reddit discussion entry for extraction, sentence-level retained quote for theme work, and interview question-answer unit for data preparation
evidence_records.Generated outputs: source relevance scores, extracted quotes, high-level theme assignments, bottom-up subthemes, quote-to-theme mappings, prevalence counts, and evidence-bearing reports
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: Extracted Reddit quotes retain submission ID/title/body summary and report themes include quotations; two researchers check three quotes per theme. In the user interface, source identifiers are masked and direct links to original posts are unavailable, limiting provenance inspection.
evidence_records.Baselines: Study 1 participants' own non-AI expert research under a short timed task; six authoritative reports yielding 22 consensus reference themes; Reddit-versus-interview source comparison; conceptual comparison to TopicGPT/LLooM/QuaLLM.
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: A different random set of 100 subreddits was used for each adaptive relevance-prompt iteration, but the number of iterations and final independent holdout are not reported; stochastic generation runs and seeds are not reported.
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: Cohen kappa for subreddit relevance calibration, manual quote-relevance agreement threshold (>70%), theme overlap/coverage counts, quote counts/prevalence, timed theme counts, Likert usability responses, and approximate latency/cost
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: Counterbalanced within-participant Study 1 with 11 experienced policy researchers comparing workflow versus own methods for 10-15 minutes per topic, plus retrospective surveys/interviews; Study 2 two-researcher consensus mapping against themes manually extracted from six reports.
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: 11 policy researchers spanning government, academia, philanthropy, health, economics, and budgeting; one/two study researchers at different validation steps; one public-polling expert
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: Subreddit relevance prompt tuned to Cohen kappa 0.7 against one researcher; quote extraction refined until >70% researcher agreement on relevance; no IRR reported for generated-theme review, report-theme extraction, equivalence mapping, or Study 1 interview thematic analysis.
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: descriptive counts/percentages and overlap; no inferential test or uncertainty estimate for theme equivalence, report coverage, or Study 1 efficiency outcomes
evidence_records.Principal results: Study 1: 7/11 rated speed positively, 8/11 ease of analysis positively, and participants found about two more themes with the workflow during the timed tasks. Study 2: Reddit and interviews each matched 16 of 22 report themes; across all sources, 31 of 35 themes appeared in Reddit or interviews. The workflow also surfaced source-specific themes, while missing themes not probed by the interview protocol.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: The system processed approximately 1,000 quotes per 10 minutes in Study 1. A complete report from 10,000 aggregated posts is estimated at $150-$300. Participants cited traditional study budgets of $4,000-$80,000, while the authors state the workflow can run for less than $1,000 on Azure; full human verification time is not costed.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: Study 1 and the interview study received institutional IRB approval (institution anonymized). Interview participants consented, were paid $16, were told not to disclose sensitive information, and had PII screened/removed; transcripts used random IDs and secure dedicated-server storage. Reddit consent and user-level deidentification/quote-searchability safeguards are discussed generally but not fully specified.
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: Prompts and interview protocol are in appendices; public source archives are named. No code repository, immutable report outputs, data release, exact analysis-model snapshot, or seed record is reported.
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: Reddit and interview representativeness; three U.S. policy topics; chatbot-versus-human interview depth; prompt-tuning error propagation and output reliability; focus on QuaLLM rather than alternative frameworks.
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Reviewer interpretation: the study explicitly declines to reevaluate QuaLLM's underlying thematic-analysis validity, yet makes application-level recovery claims. The six reports differ in questions, sampling, and purpose, so consensus theme overlap is not a gold standard; equivalence mapping lacks IRR. Researcher-defined high-level categories, one-code quote mapping, fixed/nested theme prompts, and quote-frequency counts can erase multi-theme, participant-level, minority, and negative-case structure. Adaptive kappa tuning and source-selection thresholds lack a final untouched test set. The timed user baseline is short and heterogeneous, and full human verification costs are excluded.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Direct application/extension of QuaLLM; retains its quote extraction, theme generation, and mapping logic while adding policy-oriented prompts, data-source selection, interface evaluation, and multi-source evidence.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: A high-scale testbed for participant-normalized coverage, rare-case retention, direct source provenance, cross-source confounding, and evaluation that separates theme overlap from interpretive equivalence.

evidence_records.Full citation: Jeyaganthan, Athikash; Xu, Kai; Becker, Franziska; Koch, Steffen. 2026. Co-Refine: AI-Powered Tool Supporting Qualitative Analysis. arXiv:2604.19309v1. https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19309v1.
evidence_records.Title: Co-Refine: AI-Powered Tool Supporting Qualitative Analysis
evidence_records.Authors: Athikash Jeyaganthan; Kai Xu; Franziska Becker; Steffen Koch
evidence_records.Peer-reviewed status: not peer reviewed as verified by the cutoff; no archival venue was identified
evidence_records.Citation count, source, and retrieval da: not available; the official arXiv API does not supply citation counts; checked 2026-08-24
evidence_records.Relationship/dependence family: New interactive audit system positioned against CAQDAS, CoAIcoder, CollabCoder, PaTAT, Cody, LLooM, DeTAILS, LATA, and LOGOS
evidence_records.Research objective: Design a researcher-controlled qualitative coding workbench that detects intra-code inconsistency, temporal drift, and code overlap in real time while constraining LLM feedback to deterministic evidence.
evidence_records.Claimed qualitative methodology: Human-controlled qualitative coding and support for later reflexive thematic-analysis phases, especially reviewing and defining themes.
evidence_records.Actual operationalized methodology: Researcher applies codes manually; embeddings quantify centroid similarity, oldest-versus-newest drift, and code overlap; GPT-5.2 produces constrained audit narratives and periodically synthesizes evolving code definitions; the interface supports ICR and audit history.
evidence_records.Inductive, deductive, or hybrid: supports either; the system does not itself perform primary interpretation/coding
evidence_records.Domain: generic qualitative coding; formative task on hotel-review sentiment/aspect data
evidence_records.Dataset name: Controlled synthetic consistency segments and a resampled SemEval-2016 ABSA English hotel-review subset
evidence_records.Public or restricted data: hotel dataset is public; system materials are available only on reasonable request
evidence_records.Number of participants: requirements interviews N=3; formative user study N=5; participant overlap between phases not reported
evidence_records.Sensitive-data status: public review data in evaluation; user-research transcripts/consent status not reported
evidence_records.Model family: OpenAI embeddings and GPT via Azure OpenAI
evidence_records.Exact model/version: text-embedding-3-small; GPT-5.2 for audit/reflection; separate fast Azure model for chat/facet labels not reported
evidence_records.Prompting strategy: Stage 2 receives deterministic scores, surrounding context, prior segments retrieved by recency plus MMR, and the latest code reflection; its consistency_score must lie within +/-0.15 of centroid similarity. Stage 3 triggers at 3 segments and every 3 additions, using up to 30 diverse segments.
evidence_records.Fine-tuning or adaptation: no fine-tuning reported; retrieval over user coding history and deterministic post-constraint
evidence_records.Single-agent or multi-agent: single-model interactive pipeline; no agent architecture
evidence_records.Human role: Researcher remains primary coder, can inspect scores, configure thresholds, dismiss/override alerts, merge/refine codes, and use ICR resolution; three qualitative researchers inform requirements and five participants complete a formative coding task.
evidence_records.Unit of analysis: researcher-selected text span; drift compares five oldest with five newest segments after at least ten applications
evidence_records.Generated outputs: centroid-consistency score, temporal-drift score, overlap alerts, severity/finding/action narrative, alternative-code suggestion, evolving code definition/theoretical lens/derivation trace, visualizations, and immutable history
evidence_records.Evidence/provenance mechanism: Per-user stored segment embeddings, recency/MMR retrieval, append-only ConsistencyScore/edit history, and source spans structurally link alerts to the researcher's own coding history.
evidence_records.Baselines: Feature comparison with NVivo/ATLAS.ti, CollabCoder, CoAIcoder, PaTAT, and Cody; no controlled baseline measuring actual drift reduction, coding quality, or human outcomes.
evidence_records.Number of runs or seeds: software unit/integration/end-to-end tests, controlled consistency cases, and one 30-45 minute task per formative participant; stochastic LLM reruns/seeds not reported
evidence_records.Automatic metrics: centroid cosine similarity, temporal drift = 1 - cosine(old centroid,new centroid), pairwise code-overlap cosine, alert-class compliance, modified nine-item SUS, and ICR measures exposed by the interface
evidence_records.Human-evaluation design: Three 45-60 minute requirements interviews; five convenience-sample participants complete a 30-45 minute task, modified SUS, and semi-structured interview; transcripts are thematically analyzed.
evidence_records.Number and expertise of evaluators: Requirements: three UK qualitative researchers with 3-12 years' experience. Formative study: five participants ranging from no coding experience to >50 hours, including two undergraduates, two PhD students, and one academic staff member.
evidence_records.Inter-rater reliability: not reported for interview thematic analysis; Cohen/Fleiss kappa and Krippendorff alpha are system features, not evaluation outcomes
evidence_records.Statistical analysis: descriptive SUS only; no confidence intervals, controlled comparison, drift-detection accuracy, or inferential analysis
evidence_records.Principal results: All controlled alerts matched expected hand-constructed classes and the LLM score stayed within the programmed +/-0.15 constraint. Modified SUS mean was 77.77 (individual scores 63.88-86.11). Interview themes emphasized trust through grounding, reflective friction, and desire for theoretical grounding.
evidence_records.Efficiency or cost results: No measured latency, throughput, compute, monetary cost, or human-time saving is reported.
evidence_records.Ethics and privacy treatment: Consent, ethics/IRB approval, recording/transcription procedures, participant compensation, and user-study data governance are not reported. Local LLM deployment for sensitive data is future work; the current architecture uses Azure OpenAI.
evidence_records.Reproducibility resources: Source code, prompts, evaluation data, SUS, and thematic-analysis materials are stated to be available on reasonable request; no public repository, exact fast-model deployment, immutable release, or seed record is provided.
evidence_records.Author-reported limitations: Text only; embedding-model dependence and non-English/specialized-domain risk; narrative explanations can mislead; N=3/N=5 convenience samples; controlled/synthetic pipeline testing; no longitudinal real-world or comparative drift study.
evidence_records.Additional validity concerns: Reviewer interpretation: constraining an LLM score to +/-0.15 of an embedding cosine demonstrates constraint compliance, not the validity of the cosine as intra-coder consistency or of the narrative explanation. Thresholds (0.65/0.85, five-old/five-new, overlap 0.85) are not empirically validated. Legitimate reflexive change may be flagged as error. The study does not measure whether Co-Refine improves consistency, analytical rigor, or findings, so the claim of meaningful improvement exceeds the evaluation.
evidence_records.Relationship to prior papers: Combines CAQDAS-style manual coding with embedding diagnostics, constrained LLM feedback, visual analytics, and collaboration features; unlike end-to-end systems, it intentionally leaves interpretation with the researcher.
evidence_records.Relevance to the proposed ARR project: A useful provenance/audit baseline whose unvalidated construct mapping creates an open opportunity: prospective, blinded validation of provenance-aware signals against plural expert judgments and legitimate reflexive change.

claims: The workflow can recover most planted themes/subthemes in the three synthetic datasets.
Open-weight local models can improve control and reduce privacy risks relative to third-party proprietary services.
The method may help researchers scale codebook development, subject to validation on natural data.
Agreement and blind quality judgments diverge in both directions.
For the tested model mix, the verifier showed no overall human preference.
Automation decisions should be made at code level using agreement plus independent verification rather than agreement alone.
LLMs were dependable for breadth and structured annotation but not conceptual authority.
Human validation was constitutive: it added five codes and clarified boundaries.
Overlapping trios preserved dialogic context better than isolated messages for this platform.
The tested LLMs cannot reliably replace a human annotator for these nine security codes.
Detailed definitions help initially, but additional examples/interactive clarification show diminishing and non-uniform returns.
Open-weight models outperformed the tested proprietary models in this setup.
The workflow can provide rapid, rough, complementary policy sensemaking rather than replace traditional research.
Reddit and chatbot interviews recover many themes found in selected policy reports and add source-specific concerns.
Human oversight remains essential at scope, source-selection, review, and interpretation stages.
The three-stage pipeline constrains LLM audit scores to deterministic evidence.
Users valued mathematically grounded alerts and retained control.
The system can surface drift/overlap during coding rather than post hoc.

concerns: Synthetic planted-theme recovery is not equivalent to validity on naturally occurring qualitative data.
No plural, stakeholder, or participant-grounded interpretation is evaluated.
Rater number, independence, reliability, and preregistered matching rules are absent.
Temperature zero does not substitute for repeated-run or pipeline-choice sensitivity testing.
One verifier cannot establish plurality or normative validity and provides no inter-verifier reliability.
The code-level division-of-labor thresholds are post hoc and not prospectively validated.
Corpus accounting and human-allocation descriptions are internally inconsistent across the two companion preprints.
The result is conditional on one education instrument, one platform, selected models, and a redacted data source.
No human-only codebook-development control estimates anchoring or omission caused by LLM-proposed labels.
Most validation messages were single-coded after calibration.
No repeated-run or cross-model stability analysis was performed.
Participant/user coverage and negative-case preservation are not evaluated.
The task is binary deductive annotation, not end-to-end thematic analysis.
Human consensus/review remains the assumed standard and is not source-symmetrically verified.
No stochastic repeatability, calibration, or independent naturalistic dataset replication is reported.
Human-subject ethics and API governance are absent.
The central thematic-analysis component is assumed valid from prior QuaLLM work rather than independently tested here.
Report-theme overlap is a weak construct proxy because sources and questions are not equivalent.
Quote prevalence is not participant prevalence and can be dominated by prolific users or sources.
Masked identifiers and partial quote checking limit provenance and unsupported-theme detection.
Adaptive prompt/source tuning, no repeated runs, and an unspecified analysis snapshot limit reproducibility.
Constraint adherence is tautological and does not validate qualitative consistency or interpretive quality.
No real-world drift-detection ground truth, no control condition, and no pre/post coding-quality measure are reported.
Convenience N=5 modified SUS cannot support impact or generalizability claims.
Ethics and privacy reporting are absent despite user research and cloud-model use.
Request-only artifacts and incomplete model identifiers limit reproducibility.

quality_dimensions: Strength and independence of its baselines
Availability of data, prompts, code, and model versions
Whether conclusions are proportionate to the evidence

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: Explicitly distinguishes selected thematic-analysis/codebook steps from reflexive thematic analysis.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Synthetic planted-theme data are useful for pipeline debugging but weak for claims about natural qualitative interpretation.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Stages, main LLM, RAG and temperature are described, but exact embedding/dimensionality-reduction/clustering specifications are incomplete in the main text.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: No human-natural-data or alternative computational experimental baseline.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: Manual match judgments are central, but rater count, expertise, independence and reliability are not reported.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Cosine is secondary evidence and is not validated as interpretive equivalence; planted-theme matching assumes one reference universe.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: Evaluation treats the planted theme set as the target and does not assess legitimate alternatives.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Intermediate summary points/clusters are grounded, but final theme-to-quotation provenance is not reported.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: Temperature zero is reported, but no reruns, seeds, or pipeline-choice sensitivity results are provided.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: Synthetic-data status, no-human ethics determination, local-model privacy motivation, and bias limitations are explicit.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Supplementary prompts and a generic GitHub destination are reported, but release/version specificity is incomplete.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: Natural-data claims are generally conditional, but broad transformative language exceeds a simulation-only evaluation.

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: Clearly frames deductive multi-label coding and distinguishes agreement from normative quality.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Large naturalistic corpus and complex codebook, but one platform/domain and unclear record attrition.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Prompt logic, models, temperature and protocol are described; referenced configuration appendices are absent from the supplied full text and corpus accounting is unresolved.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: Human, LLM, human-human and LLM-LLM sources are evaluated symmetrically by an independent blinded verifier.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: 855 blind comparisons are substantial, but all normative judgments come from one verifier.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Jaccard is appropriately bounded as agreement and triangulated with blind preference rather than mislabeled as quality.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: Rejects a single human gold but replaces it with one independent expert's judgments rather than a plural panel/stakeholders.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Verification is source-message grounded, but no persistent evidence provenance beyond each comparison is reported.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: Four focal models are rerun and exact-match/kappa stability is reported.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: IRB, PII removal and enterprise no-training terms are reported.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Appendix availability is claimed, but supplied full text lacks those appendices and raw data/code release is absent.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: The agreement critique is supported, but code automation categories are stronger than one-verifier/one-domain evidence warrants.

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: Carefully distinguishes adapted open/axial/selective coding from theory generation and reports human decision points.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Large naturalistic corpus with message- and conversation-disjoint human validation.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Exact model IDs, units, phase samples, prompts, human review and codebook refinement are well described.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: Independent human application tests the instrument, but no human-only development baseline isolates LLM anchoring.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: Multiple expert coders and review phases, but 88.7% of validation messages are single-coded and development-review IRR is absent.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Hierarchical set Jaccard is sensible for overlap but does not validate codebook meaning or omitted constructs.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: Reflexive memoing and boundary discussion are reported, but the output remains one consensus instrument.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Researchers inspect raw data and memo decisions; no released code-to-source provenance structure is described.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: No reruns, seed analysis or cross-model sensitivity test.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: IRB, terms, PII removal, enterprise API protections and student-writing issue are disclosed.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Codebook, prompts and synthetic scripts are available; raw data are restricted and proprietary outputs are not strictly reproducible.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: Conclusions are conditional and explicitly retain conceptual authority with humans.

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: The fixed-code annotation task is clear, but the thematic-analysis label is broader than the evaluated operation.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Unpublished data reduce contamination risk, but the corpus is small, single-experiment, and participant count is missing.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Human replacement setup, prompts, comparison cells, models and tests are described in detail despite unsnapshotted chat interfaces.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: Four human contexts, reviewer labels, four models and prompt ablations provide meaningful comparators.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: Four-human annotation/review exists, but expertise, recruitment, adjudication reliability and plurality are underreported.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Kappa handles sparse agreement better than accuracy, but agreement with reviewer labels is not interpretive validity.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: Reviewer-corrected labels are treated as the target and disagreements are not source-symmetrically evaluated.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Spreadsheet labels remain tied to source comments, but no evidence-span/rationale output is required.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: No repeated stochastic trials or seeds; live chat interfaces weaken exact replication.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: No approval, consent, deidentification or vendor-governance statement for human-experiment data.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Zenodo artifact is strong, but exact hosted model snapshots/configurations are absent.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: The main conclusion is appropriately negative and bounded to the tested technical codes.

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: Workflow steps are explicit, but the operationalized hybrid template/content analysis is labeled thematic analysis without resolving tradition differences.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Very large, multi-source data and expert users, with important representativeness caveats.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Prompts and exact selection/interview models are reported; the core analysis model is only 'GPT-4' and iteration/run details are incomplete.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: Expert own-work and policy reports provide context but are non-equivalent and do not validate the underlying thematic engine.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: Experienced N=11 users and multiple reviewers, but short tasks, small samples and missing IRR on theme judgments.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Kappa is used for adaptive calibration and overlap is descriptive; neither validates interpretive equivalence or participant coverage.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: Multiple sources and human synthesis are used, but consensus mappings and report overlap still imply one reference interpretation.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Reports include quotes, yet identifiers are masked, direct links absent, and only three quotes per theme are checked.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: No repeated generation, seed, ordering or perturbation test.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: Interview protections are strong; Reddit consent, quote searchability and user-level safeguards are only partially operationalized.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Prompts are included, but no code/data release and no exact analysis snapshot.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: Complementary-tool caveats are appropriate, but reliable-recovery language is stronger than non-equivalent overlap evidence supports.

Clarity of its qualitative methodology.rationale: Researcher-controlled coding is clear, but claims of reflexive-TA support are not operationally validated.

Appropriateness of its dataset.rationale: Synthetic cases and an unspecified hotel-review subset do not test nuanced longitudinal qualitative drift.

Transparency of its computational workfl.rationale: Equations, thresholds, triggers, retrieval, models and architecture are unusually detailed.

Strength and independence of its baselin.rationale: Only feature comparisons; no controlled outcome baseline.

Adequacy of its human evaluation.rationale: Requirements N=3 and formative N=5 are useful design evidence but inadequate for impact claims.

Validity of its automatic metrics.rationale: Arbitrary cosine thresholds and enforced score proximity are not validated against qualitative judgments or real drift.

Treatment of interpretive plurality.rationale: Human override and reflexive change are respected in design, but the consistency alarm can still pathologize legitimate change.

Evidence grounding and traceability.rationale: Source spans, stored history, retrieval and immutable audit records provide strong structural traceability.

Stability and reproducibility testing.rationale: No stochastic repeat, longitudinal field test or sensitivity analysis.

Ethics, privacy, and responsible-researc.rationale: No consent/IRB/privacy reporting for user studies; sensitive-data local deployment remains future work.

Availability of data, prompts, code, and.rationale: Materials are request-only and one Azure model is unspecified.

Whether conclusions are proportionate to.rationale: Claims of meaningful consistency improvement are not supported by a measured consistency or comparative outcome.
